document.title: Ambassador Dean Cable to Secretary of State. Subject: Meeting with Gopi Arora, June 18: Afghanistan
document.authors: U.S. Embassy New Delhi (Ambassador John Gunther Dean)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: Dean reports on Gopi Arora's briefing on his meeting with Dobrynin. Arora believes Gorbachev is committed to full withdrawal, that the PDPA is stronger than the Mujahedin claim, and that India backs Najibullah's aim of keeping extreme fundamentalists out of Kabul. He asks whether US interests parallel Zia's; Dean says the US saw no role for Najibullah.

Gopi Arora met Ambassador Dean at his house in New Delhi to discuss Afghanistan.
Arora met Anatoly Dobrynin in Moscow, discussing Afghanistan, before returning to India.

Cable from Dean to State reporting the Arora meeting and US stance of no role for Najibullah.

key_claims: Arora said Gorbachev remains committed to full Soviet troop withdrawal on the publicly announced timetable.
Arora said the PDPA would lose some provincial capitals but not collapse by late summer 1988.
Arora suggested Najibullah might become dispensable in favor of a transition government of technocrats, exiles, some mujahidin and acceptable PDPA members.
India said it backed a solution keeping extreme fundamentalists out of Kabul rather than Najibullah personally.
Arora questioned whether U.S. interests really paralleled Zia's and urged diverse sources on Afghanistan.
Indians thought the answer lay more with field commanders inside Afghanistan than Peshawar leaders.
Ambassador Dean told Arora the U.S. saw no role for Najibullah now or later.
